key_insight: Dense, fine-lamellar Fe-based amorphous coatings favor long-term corrosion resistance, while increasing humidity reduces their friction coefficient and wear rate.
engineering_relevance: Detonation-spray parameter control can help produce protective coatings for carbon steel, with service humidity also influencing wear performance.
method: Deposit Fe-based amorphous coatings on Q235 carbon steel using varied detonation-spray parameters.
Examine droplet morphology, coating microstructure, and porosity.
Evaluate long-term corrosion and tribological behavior under different humidity conditions.
evidence_signal: The abstract links higher porosity to poorer long-term corrosion resistance and reports decreasing friction and wear with increasing humidity, implicating tribochemical reactions involving Si3N4 balls and water.
watch_item: The abstract provides no numerical performance data or humidity ranges, and wear trends may depend on the Si3N4 counterface.
paper_title: Long-term corrosion behaviors and wear behavior of Fe-based amorphous coatings in different humidity environments
